questions.q: In the lesson's web app, what happens when the form is posted to the /predict route?
options: The model is retrained on the submitted values
The form values are gathered, converted to a numpy array and sent to the model, which returns a prediction
The values are stored in a spreadsheet for a data scientist to review
The page reloads without contacting the model
questions.explain: The Flask route turns form input into the array shape the model expects and returns its prediction.
questions.evidence: The form variables are gathered and converted to a numpy array.

questions.q: What is the generative AI application lifecycle?
options: A licence for using large language models
A list of approved AI vendors
A benchmark for comparing models
A framework that guides you through developing, deploying and maintaining a generative AI application
questions.explain: It structures goals, measurement, challenges and solutions across the life of an AI application.
questions.evidence: The generative AI lifecycle is a framework that guides you through the stages of developing, deploying, and maintaining a generative AI application.

options: You train the model continuously or at least frequently
You train the model only once
You train a separate model for each user
You train the model on the production server
questions.explain: Static training is simpler but the model can go stale; dynamic training keeps learning from fresh data.
questions.evidence: Static training (also called offline training ) means that you train a model only once.

options: The model only makes predictions on demand, for example when a client requests one
All predictions are computed in advance and cached
The model is retrained before every prediction
Predictions are made by people, not the model
questions.explain: Dynamic inference handles diverse, real-time requests; static inference precomputes and caches predictions.
questions.evidence: Dynamic inference (also called online inference or real-time inference) means that the model only makes predictions on demand, for example, when a client requests a prediction.

questions.q: How can you make sure a model is compatible with its serving infrastructure before release?
options: Deploy it straight to production and watch the logs
Retrain it with more data
Stage the model in a sandboxed server environment to avoid dependency conflicts
Convert it to a spreadsheet formula
questions.explain: A sandboxed staging environment surfaces dependency conflicts without affecting users.
questions.evidence: Ensure model-infrastructure compatibility by staging the model in a sandboxed server environment to avoid dependency conflicts.

questions.q: How should a production ML pipeline monitor its raw input data?
options: Only check the data once, when the model is first trained
Trust the data if the model's accuracy is high
Ask users to report bad data
Continuously check it against expected values by writing rules the data must satisfy
questions.explain: A data schema with rules (for example ratings must be 1–5) catches broken inputs early.
questions.evidence: To monitor your data, you should continuously check it against expected statistical values by writing rules that the data must satisfy.

questions.q: In MLOps model validation, when is a model considered adequate for deployment?
options: When it trains without errors
When its predictive performance is better than a certain baseline
When it is larger than the previous model
When a data scientist has run it in a notebook
questions.explain: Validation compares the candidate model against a baseline before it can replace the current one.
questions.evidence: Model validation: The model is confirmed to be adequate for deployment—that its predictive performance is better than a certain baseline.

questions.q: What are 'data values skews', and what do they call for?
options: Significant changes in the statistical properties of data — a trigger to retrain the model
Typos in column names — a trigger to rename features
Slow queries — a trigger to add servers
Missing labels — a trigger to delete the data
questions.explain: When data patterns change, the model must be retrained to capture them.
questions.evidence: Data values skews: These skews are significant changes in the statistical properties of data, which means that data patterns are changing, and you need to trigger a retraining of the model to capture these changes.

questions.q: According to the Rules of Machine Learning, what must you trust before doing imaginative machine learning?
options: Your feature engineering
Your most complex model
Your pipeline
Your users' feedback
questions.explain: Start with simple, testable infrastructure; otherwise it is hard to tell what is going wrong.
questions.evidence: it will be hard to figure out what is happening if you don’t first trust your pipeline.

questions.q: What is the best way to deal with training-serving skew?
options: Train on much more data
Use a bigger model
Stop serving the model
Explicitly monitor it so system and data changes don't introduce skew unnoticed
questions.explain: Skew between training and serving data creeps in silently unless you measure it.
questions.evidence: The best solution is to explicitly monitor it so that system and data changes don’t introduce skew unnoticed.
